verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The phone rings twice in an empty house and then stops.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Dust settles on the piano keys —
someone else's music
still humming in the wood.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Steam rises from the neighbor's kettle,
a small flag
waving over the fence.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I water the plant no one remembers planting,
green
against my better judgment.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Sunday light pools on the unmade bed —
I let it stay
a little longer than I should.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The mail slot clicks —
another letter for the man
who used to live here.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
I forward nothing,
just stack the envelopes
like a small, patient debt.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone asks if I'm settled in yet.
I say yes,
and water the plant again.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The plant, though,
keeps leaning toward the window —
nobody has to teach it that.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Some nights I catch myself
leaning the same direction,
waiting on a light I can't name.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off
before it screams —
some things know their own limit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I never learned that trick —
I let myself
boil over twice before I noticed.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Steam fades from the window glass,
and there's my own face again —
still deciding what to see.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone's shoes by the door,
worn down on the left side only —
a whole life leaning quietly.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light left on all night —
not for anyone coming home,
just habit that never got the news.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Kettle's whistle, then quiet —
the silence after
still asking to be answered.
